This is my 2nd ice machine. My first lasted about 2 years. And it was fine. But this one I love! The biggest differences that made the most impact for me are 1) The basket is patterned so the scoop will stand inside it. My previous machine had no such feature. The scoop took up a lot of space causing it to read as full when it wasn't. 2) There is a drainage hole in the bottom. This is the big one for me. Previously, to empty or clean my machine was a pain in the neck. You had to pick up the whole machine to dump out the water when not in use. This machine has a drain hole that I can slide over the edge of my counter and drain all water out and clean out the machine easily. I love it.

Purchased the ice machine to have at my home bar. The machine failed right upon opening and testing it out. Did everything that was detailed on the instructions. The first batch of ice came out very thin and flimsy easy to melt in any normal drink. Then it would not do a second batch of ice. It kept on lighting up the add more water button. The reservoir was already filled. I called customer service, I was told to empty the unit completely and drain all the water, leave the unit open and unplugged for 24 to 36 hours. I was told this would "reset" the ice machines censors. I did this. and Nope.... 36 hours later,,, same results. Just one batch of melty ice. And the unit was done. Asked if I wanted a replacement or money back. I said please send me a replacement.. 2 days later I get an email stating there is no replacements available until Sept. So I then said just please return my money. I had to then cut the cord of the unit and send 2 pics to customer service that I did that... They returned the cost of unit to me, but not the tax on it. And it took 3 weeks for the refund check to arrive.
They stand behind their product for only 30 days. So make sure to test it as soon as it arrives if you do order this ice machine. I would pass on it.

I bought this ice maker for our office of 4 people. It's perfect for our environment. We have found that making one complete batch of ice (meaning one fill up of water) takes just a few hours, and will last our office for two days. We put the extra in a container in the freezer, use it for a couple days, and then make more. After a batch is completed, we drain the unit and shut it off until we need it again.

Yes, the ice is a bit wet when it falls into the basket, and yes, it does stick together a bit when you put the extra in the freezer. It's not that bad, however. We just take a spoon and lightly break it apart. It doesn't take a lot of effort. It would be nice if the ice stayed colder while in the basket, but I'm sure the unit wouldn't be at this price point if it did that.
